segments.vo: One hundred fifty-eight million dollars. Gone in one night.

According to federal filings, Elon Musk sent one hundred fifty-eight million dollars into the fight for a single Texas Senate seat. His side lost. And the next morning, something weird happened to Tesla.
Almost every electric car stock went up. Lucid jumped twelve percent. Rivian, six. Nio, four. One went down. The company that moved its headquarters to Texas. Tesla.

So what actually changed in Texas? Is Tesla in trouble, or is this just noise? And stick around, because at the end I'll show you what ten dollars a day in Tesla, since it moved to Texas, turned into.
Headlines are saying Texas turned blue. That's only half true. Here's the scoreboard.

Democrats won the governor's office with Gina Hinojosa. They won a U.S. Senate seat with James Talarico. They won the attorney general's office. And they flipped the Texas House. But Republicans held on to the Texas Senate. So nobody in Austin can pass a law alone. Remember that. It matters for everything next.

scene.source: AP via CBS Texas, NBC DFW, Texas Tribune

segments.chapter: What Tesla has riding on Texas
segments.vo: Now here's the part most headlines skip. What does Tesla actually have riding on Texas? A lot. In October 2021, Tesla said it was moving its headquarters from California to Austin. In 2022 its giant Texas factory opened. Texas rules let driverless robotaxis run on public roads. And the state set up special business courts, where Tesla, as a Texas company, can take its legal fights.
Every one of those was built under a Republican government. So the real question on Wall Street was simple. Which of these can a new government actually touch?

segments.chapter: What can change, what probably won't
segments.vo: But here's the twist. Anything that needs a brand new law has to get through a Republican state Senate. That's a high wall. What can move faster? Who runs state agencies. What the new attorney general decides to investigate. And the appeals court that hears business cases, where Democrats also won the seats.

scene.left_note: Blocked by a GOP state Senate

segments.vo: And the new senator? Talarico has said he supports Tesla building cars in Texas. So the fight is less about the factory, and more about Elon Musk's politics.

segments.vo: So what happens next? We don't predict. But here are three ways this can go.

scene.sub: No predictions. Just what to watch.

segments.vo: One. Calm. Split government, few new laws, the factory and the robotaxi rules stay. Two. Friction. New investigations, slower permits for new projects. Three. Repricing. Investors decide Musk's politics cost money, no matter what Texas does. Watch the attorney general's first moves, the first permit fights, and whether the state Senate makes deals.
